verdict.rationale: Zapier documents its own programmatic, terminal-driven execution paths. The SDK can be installed via npm, authenticated with client credentials, and used to execute actions. The SDK CLI runs actions directly from the terminal, and agents can run them as a CLI or typed Node module. These are plausible headless primitives, but no evidence shows CI pipeline usage, non-interactive token handling for CI, or exit-code behavior. missing for 10: explicit CI/headless documentation (pipeline examples, non-interactive auth guidance for CI runners), independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Install @zapier/zapier-sdk via npm, authenticate with OAuth or client credentials, and execute actions across 9,000+ apps.
The Zapier SDK CLI lets you explore and run actions across {appCount} apps directly from your terminal, authenticated, with no OAuth setup required.
